children.name: Alauda
children.description: The Skylark's sustained spiralling song-flight — rising to a tiny dot 300 m above Swedish farmland — is one of the most celebrated sounds in northern European natural history. Populations have fallen by over half across Europe in 50 years due to changes in farming.

children.name: Alauda arvensis
children.description: The Eurasian skylark (Alauda arvensis), commonly referred to in Europe as the lark, is a passerine bird in the lark family, Alaudidae.

children.name: Alauda gulgula
children.description: The Oriental skylark (Alauda gulgula) is a species of skylark found in the Sino-Indian region and parts of central Asia.

children.name: Alauda razae
children.description: The Raso lark (Alauda razae) is a small passerine bird with a highly restricted range, being found only on Raso islet in the Cape Verde Islands.

children.name: Alauda japonica
children.description: The Japanese skylark (Alauda arvensis japonica) is a subspecies of the Eurasian skylark.

children.name: Lullula
children.description: A monotypic genus of sandy open country and heath, the Woodlark is distinguished from Alauda by its very short tail, prominent supercilia meeting at the bill, and a liquid, cascading song considered among the finest of any European passerine.

children.name: Lullula arborea
children.description: The woodlark or wood lark is the only extant species in the lark genus Lullula. It is found across most of Europe, the Middle East, western Asia and the mountains of north Africa. It is mainly resident (non-migratory) in the west of its range, but eastern populations of this passerine bird are more migratory, moving further south in winter.

children.name: Eremophila
children.description: Larks with striking black-and-yellow facial patterns and small feathered 'horns', breeding on open tundra, steppe, and desert plateaus across the Holarctic. The genus shows remarkable geographic variation, with dozens of subspecies adapted to different climatic zones.

children.name: Eremophila alpestris
children.description: The horned lark or shore lark is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found across the northern hemisphere. It is known as "horned lark" in North America for distinctive feathers on the heads of the male birds in summer, and as "shore lark" in Europe because it can be found on shorelines in the winter.

children.name: Eremophila bilopha
children.description: Temminck's lark (Eremophila bilopha) or Temminck's horned lark is a bird species of the family Alaudidae. It breeds across much of north Africa, through northern Saudi Arabia to western Iraq. It is mainly resident, but some populations of this passerine bird are partially migratory, moving further south in winter. This bird's common name commemorates the Dutch naturalist Coenraad Jacob Temminck. The population is declining in Israel and may also be declining elsewhere, probably as a result of habitat loss. Nevertheless, this is a common bird in many parts of its wide range and the International Union for Conservation of Nature has rated its conservation status as being of "least concern".

children.name: Melanocorypha
children.description: Large, robust larks of open steppe and desert from the Iberian Peninsula east across Central Asia to Mongolia and China. Many species are partly or wholly migratory, and several are characterised by conspicuous white or black-tipped wing patterns visible in flight.

children.name: Melanocorypha calandra
children.description: The calandra lark (Melanocorypha calandra) or European calandra-lark breeds in warm temperate countries around the Mediterranean and eastwards through Turkey into northern Iran and southern Russia.

children.name: Melanocorypha bimaculata
children.description: The bimaculated lark (Melanocorypha bimaculata) breeds in warm temperate countries eastwards from Turkey into Central Asia.

children.name: Melanocorypha mongolica
children.description: The Mongolian lark (Melanocorypha mongolica) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found from southern Russia and Mongolia to central China.

children.name: Melanocorypha yeltoniensis
children.description: The black lark (Melanocorypha yeltoniensis) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found in south-eastern Russia and Kazakhstan.

children.name: Melanocorypha maxima
children.description: The Tibetan lark (Melanocorypha maxima) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found on the Tibetan Plateau from north-western India to central China.

children.name: Calandrella
children.description: Small, compact short-toed larks of arid and semi-arid open country across the Palearctic, Middle East, and East Africa. The genus includes several cryptic species, best separated by voice, range, and subtle structural features.

children.name: Calandrella brachydactyla
children.description: The greater short-toed lark (Calandrella brachydactyla) is a small passerine bird.

children.name: Calandrella acutirostris
children.description: Hume's short-toed lark (Calandrella acutirostris) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae. It is found in south-central Asia from Iran and Kazakhstan to China.

children.name: Calandrella blanfordi
children.description: Blanford's lark or Blanford's short-toed lark (Calandrella blanfordi) is a small passerine bird of the lark family, Alaudidae, which is native to north-eastern Africa. Its common name commemorates the English zoologist William Thomas Blanford.

children.name: Calandrella erlangeri
children.description:
Erlanger's lark (Calandrella blanfordi erlangeri) is a small passerine bird of the lark family endemic to the highlands of Ethiopia. The name of this bird commemorates the German ornithologist Carlo von Erlanger.
It is considered to be a subspecies of Blanford's lark. Alternate names include Erlanger's red-capped lark, Erlanger's short-toed lark and Ethiopian short-toed lark.

children.name: Calandrella cinerea
children.description: The red-capped lark (Calandrella cinerea) is a small passerine bird that breeds in the highlands of eastern Africa southwards from Ethiopia and Somaliland. In the south, its range stretches across the continent to Angola and south to the Cape in South Africa.

children.name: Calandrella rufescens
children.description: thumb|Eggs of Alaudala rufescens minor [[MHNT]].

children.name: Calendulauda
children.description: African bush-larks and related savanna and scrubland species, largely confined to sub-Saharan Africa and the southern half of the continent. Many members are skulking birds of dense vegetation, detected more easily by song than by sight.

children.name: Calendulauda africanoides
children.description: The fawn-coloured lark (Calendulauda africanoides) or fawn-coloured bush-lark is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae. It is found in south-central Africa.

children.name: Calendulauda albescens
children.description: The Karoo lark (Calendulauda albescens) or red-backed lark is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae.

children.name: Calendulauda alopex
children.description: The fawn-coloured lark (Calendulauda africanoides) or fawn-coloured bush-lark is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae. It is found in south-central Africa.

children.name: Calendulauda burra
children.description: The red lark (Calendulauda burra), also known as the ferruginous lark or ferruginous sand-lark, is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae.

children.name: Calendulauda erythrochlamys
children.description: The dune lark (Calendulauda erythrochlamys) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae.

children.name: Calendulauda poecilosterna
children.description: The pink-breasted lark (Calendulauda poecilosterna) or pink-breasted bushlark is a species of passerine bird in the family Alaudidae.

children.name: Calendulauda sabota
children.description: The sabota lark (Calendulauda sabota) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae.

children.name: Calendulauda seebohmi
children.description: Barlow's Lark is a recently recognised species of coastal Namibia, separated from the Karoo Lark on the basis of plumage, song, and habitat differences. It inhabits dry, stony scrub on gravel plains close to the Atlantic coast.

children.name: Eremalauda
children.description: Small desert larks of sandy and stony wastes in North Africa, the Sahara-Sahel zone, and the Arabian Peninsula. Often pale and cryptically coloured, they are adapted to extreme aridity with a preference for sparse, wind-rippled sand surfaces.

children.name: Eremalauda dunni
children.description: Dunn's lark (Eremalauda dunni) is a small passerine bird of the lark family. It is a desert bird which is found across parts of the Sahara from Mauritania to central Sudan.

children.name: Spizocorys
children.description: Small, short-billed larks of dry grassland, steppe, and semi-arid scrub in Africa, characterised by compact build and often heavily streaked plumage. Several species are Near Threatened or restricted to the Horn of Africa.

children.name: Spizocorys conirostris
children.description: The pink-billed lark (Spizocorys conirostris) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found in southern Africa. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical dry lowland grassland. It is described as having a low breeding success rate.

children.name: Spizocorys fringillaris
children.description: Botha's lark (Spizocorys fringillaris) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae that is endemic to South Africa. It is considered to be South Africa's most endangered bird species with approximately 340 mature individuals left in the wild. Over the last decade, there has been a 90% population decline resulting in the species regionally being uplisted to Critically Endangered in the 2025 Regional Red Data Book of Birds of South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini.

children.name: Spizocorys obbiensis
children.description: The Obbia lark (Spizocorys obbiensis) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae.

children.name: Spizocorys personata
children.description: The masked lark (Spizocorys personata) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae.

children.name: Spizocorys sclateri
children.description: Sclater's lark (Spizocorys sclateri) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae. It is found in Namibia and South Africa. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical dry shrubland. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Galerida
children.description: Crested larks with prominent, always-erect crests, widespread from Western Europe and North Africa across the Middle East and South Asia to Southeast Asia. They favour open, often disturbed habitats including roadsides, cultivation margins, and semi-desert, and are largely sedentary.

children.name: Galerida cristata
children.description: The crested lark (Galerida cristata) is a species of lark widespread across Eurasia and northern Africa.

children.name: Galerida theklae
children.description: Thekla's lark (Galerida theklae), also known as the Thekla lark, is a species of lark that breeds on the Iberian Peninsula and in North and East Africa south to Kenya. It is a sedentary (non-migratory) species. This is a common bird of dry open country, often at some altitude. Thekla's lark was named by Alfred Edmund Brehm in 1857 for his recently deceased sister Thekla Brehm. The name is a modern Greek one, Θέκλα (Thekla), which comes from ancient Greek Θεόκλεια (Theokleia) derived from θεός (theos, "god") and κλέος (kleos, "glory" or "honour"). The population is declining in parts of Spain, but this is a common bird with a very wide range and the International Union for Conservation of Nature has rated its conservation status as being of "least concern".

children.name: Galerida malabarica
children.description: The Malabar lark, or Malabar crested lark (Galerida malabarica) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found in western India.

children.name: Galerida deva
children.description:
Sykes's lark (Galerida deva) is a species of lark found in the dry open country of India. Its distribution is mainly restricted to central India, although stray records have been found elsewhere on the sub-continent. It is identified by its prominent crest and its overall rufous colouration. It has streaks on its breast which are less prominent than those found in the Oriental skylark.
It can imitate the calls of 34 other birds within its habitat.

children.name: Galerida magnirostris
children.description: The large-billed lark or southern thick-billed lark (Galerida magnirostris) is a small passerine bird found in southern Africa. The name "large-billed lark" may also refer to Bradfield's lark. The name "thick-billed lark" more commonly refers to the species of the same name (i.e. Rhamphocoris clotbey).

children.name: Galerida modesta
children.description: The sun lark (Galerida modesta) or Nigerian sun lark, is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae.

children.name: Mirafra
children.description: The largest genus of larks, comprising African and Asian bush-larks of open woodland, savanna, and grassland. Many Mirafra larks are best identified by their wing-snapping display flights and elaborate, musical songs; plumage is often cryptically variable.

children.name: Mirafra angolensis
children.description: The Angola lark (Amirafra angolensis) or Angola bushlark is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found in southern and central Africa.

children.name: Mirafra ashi
children.description: The Somali lark (Corypha somalica) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae endemic to Somalia.

children.name: Mirafra cantillans
children.description: The singing bush lark or Horsfield's bush lark (Mirafra javanica) is a species of lark which inhabits grassland throughout most of Australia and much of Southeast Asia. It was described by the American naturalist Thomas Horsfield.

children.name: Mirafra cheniana
children.description: The melodious lark (Mirafra cheniana) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found in southern Africa.

children.name: Mirafra cordofanica
children.description: Kordofan lark (Mirafra cordofanica) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found in Africa.

children.name: Mirafra javanica
children.description: The singing bush lark or Horsfield's bush lark (Mirafra javanica) is a species of lark which inhabits grassland throughout most of Australia and much of Southeast Asia. It was described by the American naturalist Thomas Horsfield.

children.name: Mirafra albicauda
children.description: The white-tailed lark (Mirafra albicauda) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found in Africa.

children.name: Mirafra williamsi
children.description: Williams's lark (Mirafra williamsi) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae. Discovered in 1955, much of its life and ecology is still a mystery to ornithology.

children.name: Mirafra somalica
children.description: The Somali lark (Corypha somalica) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae endemic to Somalia.

children.name: Mirafra rufocinnamomea
children.description: The flappet lark (Amirafra rufocinnamomea) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae that is widespread across Sub-Saharan Africa.

children.name: Mirafra pulpa
children.description: Friedmann's lark (Mirafra pulpa) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found in East Africa.

children.name: Mirafra hova
children.description: The Madagascar lark (Eremopterix hova) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae endemic to Madagascar.

children.name: Mirafra affinis
children.description: Jerdon's bush lark (Plocealauda affinis) or Jerdon's lark is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found in south Asia. This was formerly placed in the genus Mirafra and considered as a subspecies of Mirafra assamica and termed as the Madras bushlark. Two other species in the complex include Mirafra marionae and Mirafra microptera. Jerdon's bush lark is typically very pale on the underside

children.name: Mirafra passerina
children.description: The monotonous lark (Mirafra passerina) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found in southern Africa.

children.name: Mirafra collaris
children.description: The collared lark (Amirafra collaris) or collared bushlark is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found in East Africa.

children.name: Mirafra harterti
children.description: Hartert's Lark is an enigmatic, little-known species from dry scrub in Somalia and adjacent areas of Ethiopia, named after the distinguished German ornithologist Ernst Hartert of the Tring Museum. It is known from very few specimens and its exact taxonomic status has been debated.

children.name: Mirafra naevia
children.description: The sabota lark (Calendulauda sabota) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae.

children.name: Mirafra fischeri
children.description: The flappet lark (Amirafra rufocinnamomea) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae that is widespread across Sub-Saharan Africa.

children.name: Mirafra albicaudatus
children.description: The Somali Bush Lark is a small, pale lark of dry acacia scrub and sandy semi-desert in Somalia and the Ogaden region of Ethiopia. It is one of several endemic or near-endemic lark species found in the Horn of Africa, a hotspot for lark diversity.

children.name: Mirafra torrida
children.description: The Kilimanjaro Lark is a little-known lark of open grasslands at moderate elevations in northern Tanzania and adjacent Kenya, in the zone around Mount Kilimanjaro and the Arusha region. It was previously treated as a subspecies of the Rufous-naped Lark.

children.name: Mirafra levaillantii
children.description: The Natal Lark is a secretive, grassland specialist of moist tall grassland in eastern South Africa, Lesotho, and Swaziland, named in honour of François Le Vaillant, the pioneering French naturalist and ornithologist who explored southern Africa in the late 18th century.

children.name: Mirafra burra
children.description: The red lark (Calendulauda burra), also known as the ferruginous lark or ferruginous sand-lark, is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae.

children.name: Mirafra sharpii
children.description: The russet lark (Corypha sharpii), also known as Sharpe's lark, is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found in Somalia.

children.name: Chersomanes
children.description: A monotypic genus of robust, long-billed larks of dry scrub and stony plains in southern Africa, close in ecology to the long-billed Certhilauda larks.

children.name: Chersomanes albofasciata
children.description:
The spike-heeled lark (Chersomanes albofasciata) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae. It is found in southern Africa.
Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry shrubland and subtropical or tropical seasonally wet or flooded lowland grassland.

children.name: Pinarocorys
children.description: Medium-sized, rather thrush-like African larks of dry open woodland and savanna, less closely associated with bare ground than most larks and more often found in lightly wooded areas.

children.name: Pinarocorys erythropygia
children.description:
The rufous-rumped lark (Pinarocorys erythropygia) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae. It is found in western and central Africa from Mali, Guinea and Sierra Leone to eastern Sudan, South Sudan and north-western Uganda. Its natural habitat is dry savannah.
Originally, the rufous-rumped lark was classified within the genus Alauda. Later, some authorities considered the rufous-rumped lark to be a species within the genera Certhilauda and Mirafra. Alternate common names include red-rumped lark, red-tailed bush lark and red-tailed lark.

children.name: Pinarocorys nigricans
children.description: The dusky lark (Pinarocorys nigricans), also known as the dusky bush lark or rufous-rumped bush lark, is a species of migratory lark in the family Alaudidae.

children.name: Ramphocoris
children.description: A monotypic genus of very large-billed larks confined to stony desert and rocky semi-desert across North Africa and the Arabian Peninsula.

children.name: Ramphocoris clotbey
children.description: The thick-billed lark (Ramphocoris clotbey) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae native to north Africa and the far southwest of Asia, in the northern Sahara and Arabian Deserts.

children.name: Ammomanes
children.description: Desert finch-larks and desert larks of sandy and rocky deserts from the Sahara across the Arabian Peninsula to South Asia, characterised by plain sandy or rufous plumage and unstreaked underparts that blend with their arid substrates.

children.name: Ammomanes cinctura
children.description: The bar-tailed lark or bar-tailed desert lark (Ammomanes cinctura) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae. Two other species, the rufous-tailed lark and the Cape clapper lark are both also sometimes referred to using the name bar-tailed lark. It is found from Morocco to Pakistan. Its natural habitat is hot deserts. This is in many places a common species, but elsewhere rather less common. It has a very wide distribution and faces no obvious threats, but surveys have shown that it is slowly decreasing in numbers. The International Union for Conservation of Nature has rated its conservation status as being of "least concern".

children.name: Ammomanes deserti
children.description: The desert lark (Ammomanes deserti) breeds in deserts and semi-deserts from Morocco to western India.

children.name: Ammomanes phoenicura
children.description: The rufous-tailed lark (Ammomanes phoenicura), also sometimes called the rufous-tailed finch-lark, is a ground bird found in the drier open stony habitats of India and parts of Pakistan. Like other species in the genus it has a large finch-like bill with a slightly curved edge to the upper mandible. The dull brown colour matches the soil as it forages for grass seeds, grain and insects. Males and females are indistinguishable in the field but during the breeding season, the male has a courtship display that involves flying up steeply and then nose-diving and pulling up in a series of stepped wavy dips accompanied by calling. They forage on the ground in pairs or small groups.

children.name: Ammomanes azizi
children.description: The Saharan Desert Lark is a recently elevated species of central Saharan rock desert, previously treated as a subspecies of Ammomanes deserti. It occupies the rocky regs and hamadas of Algeria, Libya, and Chad, where its pale sandy-grey plumage is an excellent match to the substrate.

children.name: Ammomanopsis
children.description: A monotypic genus closely related to Ammomanes, confined to the gravel plains and stony desert of Namibia and southern Angola. Previously included within Ammomanes, it is now recognised as a separate genus on the basis of molecular and morphological data.

children.name: Ammomanopsis grayi
children.description: Gray's lark (Ammomanopsis grayi) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae. It is found in south-western Africa in its natural habitat of hot deserts.

children.name: Chersophilus
children.description: A monotypic genus of Mediterranean and North African semi-deserts, closely allied to Galerida but differing in structure, song, and habitat preferences. Dupont's Lark is highly secretive and more often heard than seen.

children.name: Chersophilus duponti
children.description: Dupont's lark (Chersophilus duponti) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae of the monotypic genus Chersophilus. It is found in northern Africa and Spain.

children.name: Heteromirafra
children.description: Rare and threatened larks of specialised grassland habitats in eastern Africa and South Africa, closely related to Mirafra but separable by molecular data and highly restricted ranges. Several species have experienced significant population declines.

children.name: Heteromirafra archeri
children.description: Archer's lark (Heteromirafra archeri), also known as the Liben lark, is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae. It is found in Somalia, Somaliland, and Ethiopia. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry shrubland and subtropical or tropical dry lowland grassland. It is threatened by habitat loss. The bird's common name and binomial commemorate the British explorer and colonial official Sir Geoffrey Francis Archer.

children.name: Heteromirafra ruddi
children.description: Rudd's lark (Heteromirafra ruddi) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae. It is endemic to South Africa. Its natural habitat is high-altitude grassland. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Heteromirafra sidamoensis
children.description: Archer's lark (Heteromirafra archeri), also known as the Liben lark, is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae. It is found in Somalia, Somaliland, and Ethiopia. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry shrubland and subtropical or tropical dry lowland grassland. It is threatened by habitat loss. The bird's common name and binomial commemorate the British explorer and colonial official Sir Geoffrey Francis Archer.

children.name: Certhilauda
children.description: Long-billed larks of southern African arid and semi-arid zones, with slender, decurved bills used to probe sandy soil and rock crevices for invertebrates. Several species are endemic to the Karoo, Namaqualand, or coastal Namibia.

children.name: Certhilauda chuana
children.description: The short-clawed lark (Certhilauda chuana) or short-clawed bush-lark, is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae. It is found in Botswana and South Africa. Its natural habitat is dry savannah.

children.name: Certhilauda curvirostris
children.description: The Cape long-billed lark (Certhilauda curvirostris), also known as the Cape lark, Cape longbill or long-billed lark is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae. It is found in south-western Africa. Its natural habitats are semi-arid Karoo shrub and subtropical dry shrubland and subtropical or dry lowland and highveld grassland. This lark is also found in croplands, farmlands and coastal fynbos.

children.name: Certhilauda subcoronata
children.description: The Karoo long-billed lark (Certhilauda subcoronata) or Karoo longbill is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae. It is found in southern Africa in its natural habitat of subtropical or tropical dry shrubland.

children.name: Certhilauda semitorquata
children.description: The eastern long-billed lark (Certhilauda semitorquata), also known as the Kaffrarian long-billed lark or Eastern longbill is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae. It is found in south-eastern Africa. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical dry lowland grassland.

children.name: Certhilauda barlowi
children.description: The dune lark (Calendulauda erythrochlamys) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae.

children.name: Alaudala
children.description: Small, compact short-toed larks split from Calandrella on the basis of molecular phylogenetics, distributed across the Palearctic from the Mediterranean to Central Asia and South Asia. Many members of this genus were previously subsumed within Calandrella brachydactyla or C. rufescens.

children.name: Alaudala heinei
children.description: The Turkestan short-toed lark is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae. It is found in Ukraine and central Turkey through parts of Central Asia and southern Siberia west to south-central Mongolia and south to southern Afghanistan. This species and the Mediterranean short-toed lark were formerly considered conspecific and called the lesser short-toed lark, but a 2020 study recovered them as distinct species.

children.name: Alaudala rufescens
children.description: The Mediterranean short-toed lark is a small passerine bird found in and around the Mediterranean Basin. It is a common bird with a very wide range from Canary Islands north to the Iberian Peninsula and east throughout North Africa to parts of the Middle East. The International Union for Conservation of Nature has rated its conservation status as being of "least concern".

children.name: Alaudala raytal
children.description: The sand lark (Alaudala raytal) is a small passerine bird in the lark family, Alaudidae, found in southern Asia.

children.name: Alaudala minor
children.description: The Saharan Short-toed Lark inhabits stony desert, desert margins, and arid scrub across the central and eastern Sahara from Algeria and Libya east to Sudan. It is one of several cryptic short-toed larks of North Africa that were long subsumed within broader species concepts.
